technical-data.invention-title: IMPROVEMENTS IN A PREFABRICATED SECTIONAL RESIDENCE BLOCK
AMELIORATIONS APPORTEES A UN MONOBLOC A ELEMENTS PREFABRIQUE

addressbook.name: F A E IND ALLOGGI PREFABBRICAT

abstract.p: An improved prefabricated sectional residence block of the type having a carrying structure including a basement (S), a roof (T), and supporting angle section bars or columns (11) removably secured to basement (S) and roof (T), suitable panels forming the walls being secured to the carrying structure by section bars that can be disassembled from the outside, characterized by the fact that it is provided with a double-pitch covering (3) having a height and a shape such as to keep the overall dimension of the block unchanged, said block being able to be superimposed and/or connected to other blocks placed both parallel and perpendicular to one another so that residence rooms of any size and arrangement are formed.

L'invention concerne un monobloc à éléments préfabriqué amélioré du type pourvu d'une structure portante comprenant un soubassement (S), un toit (T), et des profilés angulaires de soutien, ou des colonnes (11), fixés de manière amovible au soubassement (S) et au toit (T). Des panneaux destinés à former des parois sont par ailleurs fixés à ladite structure portante par des profilés pouvant être démontés de l'extérieur. Ce monobloc se caractérise en outre par le fait qu'il est doté d'une couverture double-pente (3) dont la hauteur et la forme ne modifient nullement les dimensions globales de ce monobloc. Enfin, ce monobloc est capable d'être superposé et/ou raccordé à d'autres monoblocs, lesquels sont placés parallèlement et perpendiculairement les uns aux autres de manière à former des pièces habitables de n'importe quelle taille ou disposition.

description.p: Improvements in a prefabricated sectional residence block

The present invention relates to the field of the prefabricated residence rooms and particularly to a sectional block for the construction of lodgings consisting of one or more rooms by connecting and/or superimposing several blocks.

A large number of prefabricated blocks characterized by assembling and disassembling systems which are quite different from one another are known. Particularly, it is known a type of prefabricated sectional block which is provided with interchangeable walls that can be assembled and disassembled from the outside without having to remove roof and corners and capable of being transported taking up a much lower room than that of an assembled block since it is provided with a wholly flat roof which allows it to be overlapped.

A first problem of such known blocks is that, in case of their installation in sites under particularly bad weather conditions, a water infiltration from the covering may occur causing discomforts and damages both to occupants and things.

A second problem of the above-mentioned blocks is that the possibilities of connecting and combining several blocks are limited by the fact that such blocks can be coupled only by superimposing and/or placing them side by side along their long sides so that the type of the residence rooms cannot be chosen at will.
Still another drawback of such known blocks is that the flooring consists of a wooden chip panel that does not guarantee a sufficient insulation especially under rigorous climate. Therefore, one aim of the present invention is to provide a block having a covering that guarantees a perfect tightness to bad weather as well as an optimum insulation even though the capability to be moved and the readiness of installation is maintained. A second aim of the invention is to pro.idc a block characterized by a capability of being connected horizontally and/or vertically without any limit of dimension and/or arrangement of the residence rooms. Still another aim of the disclosed sectional block is to guarantee, if necessary, an optimum insulation also as far as the flooring is concerned.

Such aims are achieved according to the invention by providing a block of the type having a carrying structure including a basement, a roof, and supporting angle section bars or columns removably secured to such basement and roof, suitable panels forming the walls being secured to the carrying structure by section bars that can be disassembled from the outside, characterized by the fact that it is provided with a double-pitch covering separated from the insulating underlying panel as well as with an insulating flooring panel, and that it is capable of being placed side by side to other blocks not only parallel but also perpendicular to one another.
Particularly, such covering has a height and a shape such as to keep the overall dimension of the block unchanged.

A better understanding of the invention will ensue from the following detailed description with reference to the accompanying drawings that show only by way of a not limiting example a preferred embodiment of the invention . In the αrawings :
Fig. 1 is top plan view of the block according to the invention;
Figs. 2, 3 and 4 are details in longitudinal vertical sections along a plane A-A that show the fastening of the sheet to the covering panel;
Fig. 5 is a plan view of an example of coupled blocks;
Fig. 6 is a front, view of the coupled blocks of Fig. 5;
Figs . 7 and 8 are schematic plan views of examples for connecting the blocks according to the invention;
Fig. 9 is a schematic perspective view of the coupling among parallel and perpendicular blocks;

Figs. 10 and 12 are a longitudinal section and a cross
section of a block, respectively; and
Figs. 11 and 13 are detailed views of Figs. 10 and 12, respectively.

With reference to Figs. 1-4, the block according to the invention has an upper covering including a rectangular rigid frame T formed by four section bars 1 welded at right angles to one another and having such a section as to perform the double lu-i-lion ox carrying structure and drainage of the rain water, as better shown in Figs. 3 and 4.

A horizontal sandwich panel 2 able to guarantee the insulation of the top of the block is secured inside the rectangular frame T, while a double-pitch covering 3, preferably of zinc-plated fret sheet, is secured above such panel, said covering being capable of protecting the underlying parts from the bad weather as well as allowing rain water to flow to two opposite sides of the rectangular frame so that it can flow down into the already described section bars 1. In order to avoid the problem of water infiltration at the outlet from sheet 3 to section bars 1 of the rectangular frame, the lower ends of such fret sheet 3 are secured to a corresponding section bar 5 which is placed between such sheet and sandwich panel 2 and surrounds completely the edge of the panel itself.
C θil u invention the ridge of the covering sheet 3 does not project from the plane through the upper edge of the
above-mentioned rectangular frame T. This allows a double-pitch covering to be used while keeping the overall dimension both during the transport and the installation and use of the blocks unchanged. Advantageously a hollow space 4 is formed between sandwich panel 2 and fret sheet 3 so that the thermal exchange between the inside of the residence block and the outside is further reduced. Finally, an upper section bar 6 provided with holes for fastening any upper blocks and/or tianspo Ling che block and a lower section bar 10 able to be coupled to corresponding angle columns 11 are provided at the four corners of the rectangular frame, respectively. According to a further advantageous feature of the invention it is possible to connect several blocks of the disclosed type without any limitation of the possible combinations.

With particular reference to Figs. 5 to 9 the present invention provides two types of blocks which differ from each other in length: actually, one of them has a length which is double as long as its width. Such a construction feature is particularly important as it allows the blocks to be positioned both along the major sides and the minor sides by using blocks of the above type and positioning them perpendicular to the others, as shown in the above-mentioned figures. It should be appreciated that such a feature has a

In other words, according to the invention it is possible to provide rooms of any size by installing only the peripheral walls and suppressing the inside walls between one block and the adjoining block. The basement of the disclosed block essentially consists of a rectangular frame S on which a wooden chip panel 8 and cxoove the latter a flooring 7 preferably of PVC is located.

Like the covering disclosed above, rectangular frame S of the basement is provided at its corners with upper members 12 projecting from the upper side and capable of being coupled to the lower ends of angle columns 11, and with lower members 13 provided with holes capable of being coupled to the already disclosed section bars 6 when the blocks are superimposed. Still another new feature of the invention consists in that a further insulating sandwich panel 9 is provided under flooring 7 and wooden chip panel 8 so as to considerably improve the insulation of the block from the ground as well as increase the comfort of the occupants of the residence rooms obtained by the block according to the invention.

claim.claim-text: 1. An improved prefabricated sectional residence block of the type having a carrying structure including a basement (S) , a roof (T) , and supporting angle section bars or columns (11) removably secured to basement (S) and roof (T) , suitable panels forming the walls being secured to the carrying structure by section bars that can be disassembled from the outside, characterized D the fact that it is provided with a double-pitch covering (3) having a height and a shape such as to keep the overall dimension of the block unchanged, said block being able to be superimposed and/or connected to other blocks placed both parallel and perpendicular to one another so that residence rooms of any size and arrangement are formed.

2. The sectional block of claim 1, characterized in that said upper covering includes a rectangular rigid frame (T) formed by four section bars (1) welded at right angles to one another and having such a section as to perform the double function of carrying structure and drainage of the rain water, a horizontal sandwich panel (2) able to guarantee the insulation of the top of the block being secured to the inside of rectangular frame (T) , and a double-pitch covering (3) , preferably of zinc-plated fret sheet, being secured above such panel, said covering (3) being capable of protecting the underlying parts from the
bad weather as well as allowing rain water to flow' to two opposite sides of the rectangular frame so that it can flow down into section bars (1) .

3. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that, in order to avoid water infiltration at the outlet from sheet (3) to section bars (1) of rectangular frame (T) , the lower ends of such fret sheet (3) are secured to a corresponding section bar (5) which is placed between such sheet and sandwich panel (2) and surrounds completely the edge of the panel itself.
4. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that the ridge of the covering sheet

(3) does not project from the plane through the upper edge of the above-mentioned rectangular frame (T) , thus allowing a double-pitch covering to be used while keeping the overall dimension both during the transport and the installation and use of the blocks unchanged.

5. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that a hollow space (4) is formed between sandwich panel (2) and zinc-plated fret sheet (3) so that the thermal exchange between the inside and the outside of the residence block is further reduced.

6. The sectional block of the preceding claims,
characterized in that an upper section bar (6) provided with holes for fastening any upper block and/or transporting the block and a lower section bar (10) able to be coupled to corresponding angle columns (11) are provided at the four corners of the rectangular frame (T) , respectively.

7. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that in order to allow the connection of seveial blocks by placing them side by side both parallel and perpendicular to one another, the blocks have a length which is double as high as their width so that it is possible to arrange the residence rooms without any restrictions concerning their length and width, and to keep their capability of being connected also vertically, i.e. the capability of being superimposed on each other.

8. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that the basement of the block essentially consists of a rectangular frame (S) on which a wooden chip panel (8) and above the latter a flooring (7) is located.
9. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that rectangular frame (S) of the basement is provided at the corners with upper members

(12) projecting from the upper side and capable of being coupled to the lower ends of angle columns (11) , and with lower members 13 provided with holes capable
of being coupled to section bars (6) when the blocks are superimposed.

10. The sectional block of the preceding claims, characterized in that a further insulating sandwich panel (9) is provided under flooring (7) and wooden chip panel (8) so as to considerably improve the insulation of the block from the ground.

i . The sectional block of the preceding ciaxitib, characterized in that, in case the blocks are superimposed, the upper block is provided with a further deadening panel located between wooden chip panel (8) and insulation panel (9) ,

12. An assembly of sectional blocks according to claim 1, characterized in that there are provided in combination one or more blocks according to claim 7 and one or more blocks having the same width as the preceding blocks and any length.
